Geometric Tree Search · Research notebookSaved finite cohort · One cold invocation

Certified consequence learning · Real graph effect, shared ordinary benefit

Learned units changed the graph. Ordinary search gained the same reduction.

The complete catalogue produced \(6\) certified unit consequences, in \(6\) of \(70\) original contexts. They caused genuine extra point-candidate exclusions. Both representations reduced aggregate replay branches from \(709\) to \(686\). The point prototype was much slower than ordinary clause search; this is no distinct GCTS speed advantage.

Finite cohort completed. All \(2{,}380\) discovery/replay solves completed with no UNKNOWN. ROOT accepted the narrow finite cohort after independent saved checks. The native whole run took \(12.759901\,\mathrm{s}\) and peaked at \(36{,}323{,}328\) bytes. The broader proof-search goal remains active.
Results and costsActual marking eventsAll six refutationsAll 70 contextsParallel workNext proof-search bridge

What changed after the earlier negative result?

The earlier two-context pilot certified four clauses but changed none of its \(96\) visited paired point graphs or search sequences. Its learned guards were placed only after their clauses were already satisfied.

This follow-up declared every four-clause subset of the eight full-width signed clauses on three variables. It searched singleton boundaries, then replayed both empty and singleton boundaries. It did not select cases or consequences for later benefit. The actual result is stronger information in a few contexts, with a modest branch reduction shared by the ordinary equal-library control.

The fixed cohort and automatic rule

\[C_\sigma=\bigvee_{i=0}^{2}L_i(\sigma_i),\quad L_i(1)=X_i,\quad L_i(0)=\neg X_i,\quad |\mathcal F|=\binom84=70.\]

Clause masks are big-endian satisfying bits. All four-element subsets are retained in lexicographic order. For each original context, all six singleton boundaries are tested with the original guards active and no learned gadgets.

\[F\land(X_i=b)\models\bot\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F\models(X_i=1-b).\]

Only complete exhausted search proposes the negation of the whole fixed singleton prefix. An independent truth table certifies original-context entailment. The first two new distinct non-original certified units at most are selected in frozen order, without a benefit score or supplied proof. The actual run selected one unit in each of six contexts; the other 64 learned none.

Post-result analytical explanation. Each full-width clause excludes exactly one of the \(2^3\) three-bit assignments; four distinct clauses leave \(4\) models. A unit can hold only when those models form one coordinate half-cube. There are \(3\cdot2=6\) such half-cubes, and two independent units would leave at most \(2\) models. Thus these six formulas are one symmetry pattern under variable permutations and bit flips, not six distinct mathematical advances. This is a post-result explanation, not an expected learned count or gold fact supplied to discovery. The result is a mechanism calibration.

Replay uses the empty boundary followed by all six singletons, in all four arms. Point arms retain the same complete added tuple/guard inventory, t-supports, IDs and original active guards; only learned-R marking absent versus assigned zero differs. Ordinary arms receive exactly the same certified library. Arm position rotates by context and boundary index. The same catalogue is reused, not held out.

Same branch reduction; very different representation cost

Each empty row below contains 70 solves per arm; each singleton row contains 420. Outcomes are shown as found / exhausted / unknown. The ordinary and point exhaustions keep their distinct finite-model labels. Build, solve and per-result checking are intervals inside this one suite, not separate cold runs. The per-result checks audit complete search traces, and the separate whole-case checks include shadow diagnosis. These intervals are not measured costs of checking only a final mathematical proof.

The empty-boundary branch count was \(163\)\(\to\)\(158\) in both representations; singleton replay was \(546\)\(\to\)\(528\) in both. Point replay total was \(2.979227\,\mathrm{s}\) without and \(2.965939\,\mathrm{s}\) with units. Ordinary replay was \(0.142364\,\mathrm{s}\) and \(0.133073\,\mathrm{s}\).

These are small differences in one order-rotated suite. In particular, the \(13.288\,\mathrm{ms}\) point difference is not statistical speedup evidence. Ordinary search achieves the same aggregate branch improvement with far lower prototype overhead.

Whole-cost componentActual scopeTime
Discovery and certificationAll original singleton solves/oracle/certification, counted once\(2.509516\,\mathrm{s}\)
Whole-case and shadow verificationIndependent complete-case logic/trace/inventory and graph analysis\(2.851300\,\mathrm{s}\)
Other suite overheadSource/runtime/output/exit and other costs outside the reported nested phase totals\(1.178482\,\mathrm{s}\)
True native whole lifecycleAll work above and all replay arms; do not add nested totals again\(12.759901\,\mathrm{s}\)

The library itself cost \(2.509516\,\mathrm{s}\). Adding it to the learned point replay gives \(5.475455\,\mathrm{s}\); adding it to ordinary learned replay gives \(2.642589\,\mathrm{s}\). These accounting subtotals still omit shared whole-case and suite overhead. They are not measurements of separate cold strategies, and the observed replay savings do not repay library creation on this one catalogue.

Whole native \(12.759901\,\mathrm{s}\) stayed within the separately declared \(40\,\mathrm{s}\) cohort limit, peak \(36{,}323{,}328\) bytes within \(512\,\mathrm{MiB}\). External bracket \(12.925\,\mathrm{s}\); process 53322 exited normally and was reaped. These finite-cohort limits change none of the older Q experiments.

Two actual views of the same learned unit

The shadow checker recomposes both models from the same selected IDs, boundary, t-totals/frontier and generations. Baseline removes learned-R m-data in both the selected union and tested candidate. It does not align different actual paths or claim the baseline visited this prefix.

Across \(6{,}104\) marked graph snapshots it recorded \(36\) extra-exclusion observations, \(30\) newly singleton observations and \(6\) newly zero-degree observations. The saved-analysis author also distinguished \(36\) unique context/boundary/candidate triples and \(12\) unique context/candidate pairs. These counts have different definitions; none counts avoided CPU work.

Empty boundary: a tuple becomes unavailable

Baseline candidate port: \(1\); baseline state port: \(\ast\). The baseline/marked prefixes use identical selected IDs: R_0, R_1, R_2, R_3, R_4.

The learned guard is already selected. The forbidden tuple A_4_1 is removed; the next two actual saved events force and place A_4_0. Its placement then assigns the variable value through the shared port. This is the recorded \(2\to1\) domain change, not an invented early guard elimination.

No per-prefix candidate-check or timing counter was saved. The source extract gives whole-solve work separately; no cost is attributed to this individual exclusion. Coordinates are exact saved integers, spacing schematic, and line crossings add no values.

The next bridge returns to symbolic proof search

This complete tiny cohort resolves the mechanism question positively: certified units can add point-graph information. It also shows equal ordinary information benefit and substantial representation overhead. The next research comparison should return to arithmetic, Hilbert and receptor-family proof search, rather than stack more favorably selected easy pilots.

Keep original hypotheses and full candidate grammar, authenticate every hypothesis occurrence, preserve base fallback, and independently check an automatically generated original-target primitive word. Candidate-family or lemma guidance must be compared against an ordinary equal-information control on the same checked-proof endpoint, including discovery, construction, search and verification costs. No supplied proof route is part of this bridge.

A failed bounded model or budget stop is not a theorem that a logical target has no proof. Unproved restrictions cannot acquire proof authority. The current finite unit-point calibration has pre-grounded fixed-orientation identity_only singleton supports, no runtime translation generator, fractional/shared positive support or general growth qualification. It is no fixed universal Wang inventory, RL result, new arithmetic/Hilbert theorem or full-master/whole-goal acceptance.
